transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora. I've completed your post-cataract surgery follow-up check today.

Do you have any questions about your surgery or your recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi, yes, I do have a few questions. First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a good question. You should avoid any exercise for the first week after surgery. After that week, you can go back to light exercise like gardening, so that should be fine for you.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Great, thanks for letting me know. I was also wondering, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a good question. If you were using eye drops or gel for dry eyes before your operation, it's safe to continue using them unless you've been told otherwise by your doctor.

So you should be fine to keep using it as you were before. If you're not sure or have any concerns, it's best to check with your care team.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks, that clears it up. Another thing I've noticed is that I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended:
Yes, that can be normal. It's common for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, we'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside.

However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to check it further. In that case, please contact your care team.

Do you have any other questions?
transcript.delivered: Yes, that can be normal. It's common for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, we'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It's common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after surgery, and it should improve quickly and settle down over time.

How long ago was your surgery? If your vision is still quite blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything's okay.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you for the information. My surgery was about a week ago, so I’ll keep an eye on it. I don't have any more questions for now. Thank you for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: That's great! So just to confirm - have all your questions been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, all my questions have been answered. Thanks again!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're welcome! Take care, and don't hesitate to get in touch if you need anything else.
